- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak for 2–3 periods.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is rising, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon, model fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in subsequent periods.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often underestimates late-period price action; add 0.5–1.5% to final 5–7 days if sentiment remains positive.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending, model lags; forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–2% for each 3–5 day lag in sentiment direction.
